items.explanation: 80-year-old woman with persistent atrial fibrillation documented at every cardiology clinic visit (most recently 5/28/2026). CHA2DS2-VASc 9 (CHF/hypertensive heart disease with heart failure, hypertension, age >=75 = 2, diabetes, prior cerebral infarction/TIA = 2, coronary atherosclerosis and old MI, female). No anticoagulant is ordered or listed as a current medication - she takes only aspirin 81 mg and atorvastatin - so guideline-recommended oral anticoagulation is missing and needs review.

On citalopram 40 mg daily (current order 5/29/2026; 40 mg also exceeds the usual maximum for QT risk). Most recent ECG (11/10/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 70 bpm, QRS 118 ms, QT ~480 ms and QTc (Bazett) ~520 ms - >=500 ms, so prescriber review is required. Potassium 4.5 mEq/L (1/21/2026); most recent magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (12/1/2023).

On escitalopram 10 mg daily (current order 7/8/2026, QT watch-list drug). His only/most recent ECG (3/8/2026) shows sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with RBBB (QRS 126 ms) and a grossly prolonged, broad T wave: QT roughly 750 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 800 ms (the T wave runs nearly into the following P wave), far above the 500 ms review threshold. Potassium 4.5 mEq/L, magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (4/8/2026).

95-year-old woman on amiodarone 200 mg daily (current order 8/22/2026) with warfarin for atrial fibrillation/flutter. Her most recent ECG (4/27/2022) shows sinus rhythm at 59 bpm with QT ~540 ms and QTc (Bazett) ~535 ms, above the 500 ms threshold requiring prescriber review; QTc also rose by >130 ms from the 4/6/2022 tracing. Potassium 4.1 mEq/L and magnesium 1.8 mg/dL (2/14/2026) - magnesium is at the low end.

Citalopram 40 mg daily was started at the 3/2/2026 cardiology clinic visit. Because the start is on/after 3/1/2026 the revised memo requires an ECG within 14 days (due 3/16/2026). A 12-lead ECG was recorded 3/7/2026 (sinus rhythm, QTc ~358 ms), so the requirement was met.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily was started at the 11/10/2025 cardiology clinic visit. The 9/1/2025 memo applies (start before 3/1/2026), so an ECG was required within 30 days, due 12/10/2025. An ECG was obtained 11/24/2025, within the window, so the monitoring requirement was met (that ECG showed QTc ~510 ms and is flagged separately).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the 2/12/2026 cardiology clinic visit. The start predates 3/1/2026, so the 30-day window of the 9/1/2025 memo applies (due 3/14/2026). An ECG was obtained 3/8/2026 (24 days), within the window, so the requirement was met; that ECG shows a markedly prolonged QTc and is flagged separately.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the 4/10/2026 cardiology clinic visit, so the revised memo requires an ECG within 14 days (due 4/24/2026). The only ECG in the chart was recorded 4/29/2026 - 19 days after the start - so no ECG was obtained within the required window and the requirement was not met by the due date.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the 8/1/2026 cardiology clinic visit; an ECG was required within 14 days (due 8/15/2026). The only ECG in the chart is from 12/25/2025, before the start, and no ECG has been done since, so the follow-up ECG is overdue.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the 8/10/2026 cardiology clinic visit, so an ECG was due within 14 days (8/24/2026). No ECG is in the chart, but the 8/25/2026 telephone note records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 8/18/2026 - inside the window - and the report has been requested but not received. That outside tracing could satisfy the requirement, so completion cannot be determined until it arrives.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily was started at the 9/15/2026 cardiology clinic visit, so an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 9/29/2026. No ECG has been done yet (last tracings are from March 2025), but the window is still open as of 9/24/2026, so the requirement is not yet due.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation (coded diagnosis, repeated in every clinic note). CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (age 65-74, hypertension, coronary atherosclerosis as vascular disease). Only current medication is tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily; no anticoagulant is ordered, so recommended oral anticoagulation is missing. History of hemorrhage complicating a procedure is remote and not documented as a current contraindication, so this needs prescriber review.

At the 9/1/2026 cardiology clinic visit Dr. Kessler documented INR 1.6 and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily. The 3/1/2026 memo requires an INR within 7 days of a dose change by a clinic clinician (due 9/8/2026). INR 2.3 was resulted 9/5/2026, within the window, so the requirement was met.

On 9/10/2026 the anticoagulation clinic pharmacist decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily for a home INR of 3.4 (a dose change permitted by the clinic standing order). An INR was therefore required within 7 days, by 9/17/2026. The most recent INR in the chart is 2.6 from 8/22/2026, so the post-change INR has not been done and is overdue as of 9/24/2026.

71-year-old woman with coded paroxysmal atrial fibrillation and prior embolic cerebral infarction with residual left hemiparesis. CHA2DS2-VASc 5 (age 65-74, female, hypertension, prior stroke = 2). Current medications are carvedilol, metoprolol and famotidine only; no anticoagulant is ordered. Her most recent ECG (3/14/2025) is sinus rhythm, which does not remove the indication in paroxysmal AF.

48-year-old man with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation documented in every cardiology clinic note (most recently 6/12/2026). CHA2DS2-VASc 2 (heart failure - coded acute systolic/congestive heart failure - and hypertension), which meets the guideline threshold for recommended oral anticoagulation in men. Current medications are famotidine and pantoprazole only; warfarin was given during a hospital stay in 2025 but no anticoagulant is currently ordered.

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily was re-ordered on 8/20/2026 (valid through 12/28/2026) and is listed as a current medication, even though outside records reviewed 8/12/2026 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (hemoglobin nadir 6.9, 2 units transfused) with apixaban held at discharge pending cardiology review. The anticoagulant should not continue without that review, particularly with concurrent aspirin and clopidogrel.

Two different oral anticoagulants are current: rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (ordered 7/15/2026, valid to 12/25/2026) and apixaban 5 mg twice daily (ordered 7/15/2026, valid to 12/26/2026). The 7/15/2026 clinic note says the plan was to switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban, but rivaroxaban was not stopped and both appear on the current medication list, giving duplicate anticoagulation and a high bleeding risk.

The 6/10/2026 clinic note states "ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72". Both ECGs recorded that day (17:13 and 19:36) show atrial fibrillation with no organised P waves and an irregularly irregular ventricular response at 142-144 bpm (RR 348-720 ms). The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day tracings.

On escitalopram 10 mg daily (current order 4/23/2026, a QT watch-list drug). His most recent ECG (10/8/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QT ~475 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~506 ms, which is >=500 ms and therefore requires prescriber review per the QT monitoring memo. Potassium 4.1 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (8/23/2025) are normal. Note the 5/14/2024 clinic note describes this same tracing as "QT acceptable".

On amiodarone 200 mg daily (current order 7/29/2026, QT watch-list drug) plus warfarin for atrial fibrillation. Most recent ECG (11/24/2025, two weeks after amiodarone was started) shows sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with QT ~500 ms and QTc (Bazett) ~510 ms, at/above the 500 ms threshold requiring prescriber review. Potassium 4.4 mEq/L and magnesium 2.2 mg/dL (4/20/2026) are normal.

interpretations.explanation: Sinus rhythm at 81 bpm with a consistent upright P wave before every QRS (PR 180 ms). QRS 86 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis about +49 degrees (normal). QT ~310 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~358 ms. No prior ECG is available for comparison. Matches the 3/7/2026 clinic note ("ECG today: sinus rhythm").

Sinus rhythm at 104 bpm, regular, with an upright P wave before every QRS (PR ~138 ms). QRS 98 ms without bundle branch block, axis about +39 degrees, QTc (Bazett) ~431 ms. Prior ECG 6/20/2025 showed sinus tachycardia at 147 bpm with QTc ~413 ms; no change in rhythm or conduction and QTc change <60 ms. Note this patient has documented paroxysmal atrial fibrillation even though both tracings are sinus.

Sinus tachycardia at 110 bpm, regular (RR 540-616 ms); a discrete P wave precedes each QRS on the descending limb of the preceding T wave, PR ~130 ms. QRS 90 ms, axis about +36 degrees, QTc (Bazett) ~430 ms. Only ECG in the chart, so no comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean 144 bpm: no organised atrial activity and grossly irregular RR intervals (348-650 ms). No measurable PR interval. QRS 100 ms, axis about 0 degrees, QTc (Bazett) ~425 ms. The tracing 2 hours earlier the same day was also atrial fibrillation at 142 bpm (QTc ~428 ms), so there is no change. Both contradict the same-day clinic note describing "normal sinus rhythm, rate 72".

Sinus rhythm at 69 bpm (RR 864-884 ms) with a single late ectopic beat; P waves precede each sinus QRS with PR ~155 ms. QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis about -25 degrees (within the normal range but leftward). QTc (Bazett) ~423 ms. Prior ECG 4/27/2025 was also sinus rhythm (60 bpm, QTc ~392 ms, markedly different lead placement/extreme axis); rhythm, conduction and QTc are otherwise unchanged.
Sinus rhythm at 97 bpm, regular, with P waves before every QRS and a short PR of ~118 ms. QRS 76 ms, axis about 0 to +5 degrees, QTc (Bazett) ~403 ms. No prior ECG available.

Sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, regular, P wave before each QRS with PR ~142 ms. QRS 84 ms with no bundle branch block, axis about +20 degrees, QTc (Bazett) ~394 ms. This is the only ECG in the chart; it predates the escitalopram start of 8/1/2026, so it cannot serve as the required post-start tracing.

Atrial fibrillation with a controlled ventricular response, mean 59 bpm: no discernible P waves and irregularly irregular RR intervals (694-1164 ms). No measurable PR. QRS 94 ms, axis about +26 degrees, QTc (Bazett) ~466 ms. Three days earlier (11/12/2024) the rhythm was sinus at 69 bpm with clear P waves and QTc ~375 ms, so this shows new atrial fibrillation and a QTc increase of about 90 ms.

Sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm, regular, with a prominent P wave before each QRS (PR ~110 ms). QRS 88 ms, axis about +60 degrees, QTc (Bazett) ~391 ms. Prior ECG the previous day (3/8/2025) was also sinus at 62 bpm with QTc ~428 ms - no change in rhythm or conduction and QTc change <60 ms. Both tracings predate the 9/15/2026 haloperidol start.
Sinus rhythm at 83 bpm, very regular (RR 716-724 ms), P wave before every QRS with PR ~150 ms. Narrow QRS of 74 ms, axis about +55 degrees, QTc (Bazett) ~383 ms. No prior ECG for comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 77 bpm, regular, with large upright P waves before every QRS (PR ~155 ms). QRS 72 ms, axis about +65 degrees, QT ~415 ms with QTc (Bazett) ~470 ms (borderline prolonged but below 500 ms). Prior ECG 2/2/2020 was sinus at 76 bpm with ventricular ectopy and QTc ~497 ms: no change in rhythm or conduction and QTc change <60 ms.

Sinus tachycardia at 120 bpm, regular (RR 494-504 ms), P wave before each QRS with PR ~188 ms. QRS 96 ms, axis about +53 degrees, QTc ~366 ms. Compared with 9/16/2016 (sinus rhythm 108 bpm, QRS 108 ms, QTc ~390 ms) there is no change in rhythm, no new conduction block and QTc is within 25 ms.

Sinus bradycardia at 54 bpm with a P wave before every QRS but a prolonged PR interval of about 216 ms - first-degree AV block. QRS 84 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis near 0 to +35 degrees (normal), QTc (Bazett) ~375 ms. Prior ECG 11/30/2024 was sinus at 51 bpm with PR ~186 ms and QTc ~351 ms; rhythm unchanged, no new bundle branch block and QTc change <60 ms.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean 151 bpm: no organised P waves and chaotic RR intervals (312-602 ms). No measurable PR interval. QRS 108 ms (no complete bundle branch block), axis about 0 degrees, QTc (Bazett) ~412 ms using the median RR. The tracing from the previous evening (9/12/2025) showed sinus rhythm at 77 bpm with clear P waves, so this is new atrial fibrillation.

Sinus rhythm at 73 bpm, regular with only minor variation, P wave before each QRS (PR ~166 ms). QRS 94 ms, axis about +10 degrees, QT ~340 ms and QTc (Bazett) ~373 ms. Two days earlier (11/21/2025) the rhythm was also sinus but with frequent ectopy and a much longer QT (QTc ~514 ms), so QTc has fallen by well over 60 ms. Consistent with the 11/23/2025 note "ECG today: sinus rhythm".

Sinus rhythm at 74 bpm with a P wave before every QRS, PR ~186 ms (upper normal). QRS 96 ms with no bundle branch block, axis about +55 degrees, QTc (Bazett) ~412 ms. Only ECG in the chart, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus tachycardia at 112 bpm, regular (RR 536-540 ms), with a P wave before each QRS, PR ~165 ms. QRS 102 ms - no complete bundle branch block despite very tall precordial voltages - axis about +37 degrees, QTc (Bazett) ~383 ms. Prior ECG 7/4/2022 was also sinus at 115 bpm with QTc ~385 ms: no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc. Note the coded atrial flutter history is not evident on either tracing.

Sinus rhythm at 61 bpm with one ventricular ectopic beat and compensatory pause. Every sinus QRS is preceded by a broad P wave with a prolonged PR of about 215 ms - first-degree AV block. QRS 104 ms (no complete bundle branch block), frontal axis about -25 to -30 degrees (borderline normal/left). The T wave is broad and late: QT ~520 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~528 ms, i.e. markedly prolonged; she is not on a QT watch-list drug, but this deserves attention. No prior ECG for comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 69 bpm, regular, with a (negative in lead II) P wave before each QRS and PR ~145 ms. QRS 92 ms with no bundle branch block. Net QRS forces are directed superiorly and rightward with an axis of about -172 degrees (extreme axis deviation; lead/limb reversal should be excluded). QTc (Bazett) ~365 ms. Only ECG in the chart. Recorded 4/29/2026, 19 days after escitalopram was started, i.e. outside the required 14-day window.

Sinus rhythm at 70 bpm, regular, P wave before every QRS with PR ~155 ms. QRS is slightly widened at 118 ms with a small terminal r in V1 (incomplete right bundle branch pattern - below the 120 ms threshold for complete block). Axis about +45 degrees. QT ~480 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~520 ms - prolonged, on citalopram 40 mg daily. Prior ECG 6/17/2020 was sinus at 132 bpm with QTc ~413 ms, so QTc has increased by more than 100 ms.

Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, regular, with a P wave before each QRS (PR ~150 ms). QRS is 126 ms with a terminal positive deflection in V1 and terminal S waves in I and V6 - complete right bundle branch block. Axis about +50 degrees. The T wave is enormous and extremely prolonged, still repolarising when the next P wave arrives: QT is roughly 750 ms, giving a Bazett QTc of about 800 ms - grossly prolonged in a patient on escitalopram (flagged separately for prescriber review). Only ECG in the chart, so no comparison.

Sinus bradycardia at 54 bpm (RR 1112-1160 ms) with two late ectopic beats; P waves precede the sinus QRS complexes with PR ~176 ms. QRS 94 ms, axis about -5 degrees, QTc (Bazett) ~358 ms. Prior ECG 12/13/2018 was sinus at 66 bpm with PR ~200 ms, QRS 104 ms and QTc ~374 ms: rhythm unchanged, no new bundle branch block, QTc change <60 ms.

Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, PR 128 ms, QRS 92 ms, axis about +45 degrees. The T wave is markedly late and broad (peak ~360 ms after the R wave): QT ~475 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~506 ms - above 500 ms. The prior tracing (11/23/2022) had QTc ~342 ms at 75 bpm, so QTc has increased by well over 60 ms while on escitalopram; flagged for prescriber review.

Sinus tachycardia at 141 bpm: the RR intervals are regular (402-454 ms) and a single P wave of identical morphology precedes every QRS (PR ~120 ms); there is one atrial deflection per ventricular beat, so this is not 2:1 flutter. QRS 84 ms, axis about 0 degrees, QTc (Bazett) ~397 ms. Two days earlier (7/11/2022) the rhythm was atrial fibrillation with an irregularly irregular response at ~112 bpm, so the atrial fibrillation has resolved (converted to sinus).

Sinus rhythm at 82 bpm, regular, with a P wave before each QRS (PR ~158 ms). QRS 104 ms - slightly wide but below the threshold for bundle branch block - axis about +30 degrees, QTc (Bazett) ~425 ms. Only ECG in the chart.

Sinus rhythm at 91 bpm, regular, with a biphasic P wave in V1 before every QRS and PR ~150 ms. QRS 82 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis about -10 to -20 degrees (normal). QTc (Bazett) ~398 ms. Prior ECG 5/16/2021 was sinus at 87 bpm with PR ~146 ms and QTc ~373 ms: no change in rhythm or conduction and QTc change <60 ms.

Sinus rhythm at 61 bpm with a broad P wave before each QRS and a prolonged PR of about 212 ms (first-degree AV block). QRS is 132 ms with a QS pattern in V1-V3 and a broad, late-peaking R wave in I, aVL and V5-V6 - left bundle branch block. Frontal axis about -20 to -25 degrees. QTc (Bazett) ~432 ms (QT prolongation is partly secondary to the wide QRS). Prior ECG 6/3/2024 was identical in character (sinus 68 bpm, PR ~214 ms, QRS 132 ms with LBBB, QTc ~444 ms), so there is no change.

Sinus rhythm at 102 bpm, regular, P wave before every QRS with PR ~142 ms. QRS 88 ms, axis about +45 degrees, QTc (Bazett) ~416 ms. The tracing from the previous day (3/18/2025) is essentially identical (sinus 102 bpm, QTc ~408 ms): no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Baseline sinus rhythm at about 70 bpm (dominant RR 900-930 ms) with frequent premature atrial beats producing short cycles of 350-650 ms; low-amplitude P waves precede the sinus beats (PR ~150 ms) and the tracing is noisy. QRS 92 ms with no bundle branch block, axis about -25 degrees, QTc (Bazett) ~391 ms. No prior ECG for comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 59 bpm (RR 970-1100 ms) with one early ectopic beat; a biphasic P wave precedes each sinus QRS with PR ~192 ms. QRS 88 ms, axis about +35 degrees. The T wave is broad and late: QT ~540 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~535 ms - markedly prolonged on amiodarone. Three weeks earlier (4/6/2022) the rhythm was atrial fibrillation at ~129 bpm with QTc ~399 ms, so atrial fibrillation has resolved and QTc has increased by more than 60 ms.

Sinus tachycardia at 107 bpm, regular (RR 556-560 ms), with a P wave before each QRS and PR ~155 ms. QRS 88 ms, axis about +50 degrees, QTc (Bazett) ~403 ms. Prior ECG 7/27/2019 was sinus at 75 bpm with QTc ~409 ms: no change in rhythm or conduction and no significant QTc change.

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm, perfectly regular (RR 492-500 ms) with a P wave before each QRS (PR ~135 ms). QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block, axis about +65 degrees, QTc (Bazett) ~397 ms. This is the only ECG in the chart, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus rhythm at 102 bpm with PR 140 ms, QRS 90 ms, axis about +59 degrees and QTc (Bazett) ~397 ms. Identical to the tracing recorded 34 seconds earlier (100 bpm, QTc ~391 ms): same rhythm, no conduction abnormality and no significant QTc change.

Sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm, regular, with P waves before every QRS (PR ~168 ms). QRS 92 ms, axis about +36 degrees, QT ~420 ms with QTc (Bazett) ~391 ms. Prior ECG 5/22/2023 also sinus rhythm (57 bpm with one atrial ectopic beat, QTc ~377 ms): no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm (RR 492-496 ms) with a P wave before each QRS, PR ~130 ms. QRS has narrowed to 96 ms with only a small terminal r in V1 (incomplete right bundle branch pattern, not a complete block); net QRS forces are rightward, axis about +137 degrees (right axis deviation). QTc (Bazett) ~400 ms. On the earlier tracing the same morning (01:33) there was complete right bundle branch block with QRS 160 ms and QTc ~442 ms, so the bundle branch block has resolved and QTc changed by less than 60 ms.

Sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with one early (ectopic) beat and compensatory pause; P waves precede the sinus beats with PR ~176 ms. QRS 98 ms, axis about +66 degrees. The T wave is broad and late: QT ~500 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~510 ms. Prior ECG 6/7/2025 showed sinus bradycardia at 47 bpm with QTc ~398 ms, so QTc has risen by >100 ms after amiodarone was started on 11/10/2025.

Atrial fibrillation: no P waves are identifiable anywhere in the cycle and the ventricular response is irregularly irregular (RR 386-1092 ms, mean rate ~102 bpm). No measurable PR interval. QRS 82 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -55 degrees (left axis deviation). QTc (Bazett) ~415 ms using the median RR. No earlier ECG for comparison.

Sinus tachycardia at 120 bpm, regular (RR 494-504 ms), P wave before each QRS with PR ~188 ms. QRS 96 ms, axis about +53 degrees, QTc ~366 ms. Compared with 9/16/2016 (sinus rhythm 108 bpm, QRS 108 ms, QTc ~390 ms) there is no change in rhythm, no new conduction block and QTc is within 25 ms.

Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, PR 128 ms, QRS 92 ms, axis about +45 degrees. The T wave is markedly late and broad (peak ~360 ms after the R wave): QT ~475 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~506 ms - above 500 ms. The prior tracing (11/23/2022) had QTc ~342 ms at 75 bpm, so QTc has increased by well over 60 ms while on escitalopram; flagged for prescriber review.

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm, perfectly regular (RR 492-500 ms) with a P wave before each QRS (PR ~135 ms). QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block, axis about +65 degrees, QTc (Bazett) ~397 ms. This is the only ECG in the chart, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus rhythm at 102 bpm with PR 140 ms, QRS 90 ms, axis about +59 degrees and QTc (Bazett) ~397 ms. Identical to the tracing recorded 34 seconds earlier (100 bpm, QTc ~391 ms): same rhythm, no conduction abnormality and no significant QTc change.

Sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm, regular, with P waves before every QRS (PR ~168 ms). QRS 92 ms, axis about +36 degrees, QT ~420 ms with QTc (Bazett) ~391 ms. Prior ECG 5/22/2023 also sinus rhythm (57 bpm with one atrial ectopic beat, QTc ~377 ms): no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm (RR 492-496 ms) with a P wave before each QRS, PR ~130 ms. QRS has narrowed to 96 ms with only a small terminal r in V1 (incomplete right bundle branch pattern, not a complete block); net QRS forces are rightward, axis about +137 degrees (right axis deviation). QTc (Bazett) ~400 ms. On the earlier tracing the same morning (01:33) there was complete right bundle branch block with QRS 160 ms and QTc ~442 ms, so the bundle branch block has resolved and QTc changed by less than 60 ms.

Sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with one early (ectopic) beat and compensatory pause; P waves precede the sinus beats with PR ~176 ms. QRS 98 ms, axis about +66 degrees. The T wave is broad and late: QT ~500 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~510 ms. Prior ECG 6/7/2025 showed sinus bradycardia at 47 bpm with QTc ~398 ms, so QTc has risen by >100 ms after amiodarone was started on 11/10/2025.

arguments.explanation: Atrial fibrillation: no P waves are identifiable anywhere in the cycle and the ventricular response is irregularly irregular (RR 386-1092 ms, mean rate ~102 bpm). Sinus rhythm at 104 bpm, regular, with an upright P wave before every QRS (PR ~138 ms). QRS 98 ms without bundle branch block, axis about +39 degrees, QTc (Bazett) ~431 ms. Prior ECG 6/20/2025 showed sinus tachycardia at 147 bpm with QTc ~413 ms; no change in rhythm or conduction and QTc change <60 ms. Note this patient has documented paroxysmal atrial fibrillation even though both tracings are sinus.

Sinus tachycardia at 110 bpm, regular (RR 540-616 ms); a discrete P wave precedes each QRS on the descending limb of the preceding T wave, PR ~130 ms. QRS 90 ms, axis about +36 degrees, QTc (Bazett) ~430 ms. Only ECG in the chart, so no comparison.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean 144 bpm: no organised atrial activity and grossly irregular RR intervals (348-650 ms). No measurable PR interval. QRS 100 ms, axis about 0 degrees, QTc (Bazett) ~425 ms. The tracing 2 hours earlier the same day was also atrial fibrillation at 142 bpm (QTc ~428 ms), so there is no change. Both contradict the same-day clinic note describing "normal sinus rhythm, rate 72".

Sinus rhythm at 69 bpm (RR 864-884 ms) with a single late ectopic beat; P waves precede each sinus QRS with PR ~155 ms. QRS 84 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis about -25 degrees (within the normal range but leftward). QTc (Bazett) ~423 ms. Prior ECG 4/27/2025 was also sinus rhythm (60 bpm, QTc ~392 ms, markedly different lead placement/extreme axis); rhythm, conduction and QTc are otherwise unchanged.
Sinus rhythm at 97 bpm, regular, with P waves before every QRS and a short PR of ~118 ms. QRS 76 ms, axis about 0 to +5 degrees, QTc (Bazett) ~403 ms. No prior ECG available.

Sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, regular, P wave before each QRS with PR ~142 ms. QRS 84 ms with no bundle branch block, axis about +20 degrees, QTc (Bazett) ~394 ms. This is the only ECG in the chart; it predates the escitalopram start of 8/1/2026, so it cannot serve as the required post-start tracing.

Atrial fibrillation with a controlled ventricular response, mean 59 bpm: no discernible P waves and irregularly irregular RR intervals (694-1164 ms). No measurable PR. QRS 94 ms, axis about +26 degrees, QTc (Bazett) ~466 ms. Three days earlier (11/12/2024) the rhythm was sinus at 69 bpm with clear P waves and QTc ~375 ms, so this shows new atrial fibrillation and a QTc increase of about 90 ms.

Sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm, regular, with a prominent P wave before each QRS (PR ~110 ms). QRS 88 ms, axis about +60 degrees, QTc (Bazett) ~391 ms. Prior ECG the previous day (3/8/2025) was also sinus at 62 bpm with QTc ~428 ms - no change in rhythm or conduction and QTc change <60 ms. Both tracings predate the 9/15/2026 haloperidol start.
Sinus rhythm at 83 bpm, very regular (RR 716-724 ms), P wave before every QRS with PR ~150 ms. Narrow QRS of 74 ms, axis about +55 degrees, QTc (Bazett) ~383 ms. No prior ECG for comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 77 bpm, regular, with large upright P waves before every QRS (PR ~155 ms). QRS 72 ms, axis about +65 degrees, QT ~415 ms with QTc (Bazett) ~470 ms (borderline prolonged but below 500 ms). Prior ECG 2/2/2020 was sinus at 76 bpm with ventricular ectopy and QTc ~497 ms: no change in rhythm or conduction and QTc change <60 ms.

Sinus tachycardia at 120 bpm, regular (RR 494-504 ms), P wave before each QRS with PR ~188 ms. QRS 96 ms, axis about +53 degrees, QTc ~366 ms. Compared with 9/16/2016 (sinus rhythm 108 bpm, QRS 108 ms, QTc ~390 ms) there is no change in rhythm, no new conduction block and QTc is within 25 ms.

Sinus bradycardia at 54 bpm with a P wave before every QRS but a prolonged PR interval of about 216 ms - first-degree AV block. QRS 84 ms with no bundle branch block, frontal axis near 0 to +35 degrees (normal), QTc (Bazett) ~375 ms. Prior ECG 11/30/2024 was sinus at 51 bpm with PR ~186 ms and QTc ~351 ms; rhythm unchanged, no new bundle branch block and QTc change <60 ms.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean 151 bpm: no organised P waves and chaotic RR intervals (312-602 ms). No measurable PR interval. QRS 108 ms (no complete bundle branch block), axis about 0 degrees, QTc (Bazett) ~412 ms using the median RR. The tracing from the previous evening (9/12/2025) showed sinus rhythm at 77 bpm with clear P waves, so this is new atrial fibrillation.

Sinus rhythm at 73 bpm, regular with only minor variation, P wave before each QRS (PR ~166 ms). QRS 94 ms, axis about +10 degrees, QT ~340 ms and QTc (Bazett) ~373 ms. Two days earlier (11/21/2025) the rhythm was also sinus but with frequent ectopy and a much longer QT (QTc ~514 ms), so QTc has fallen by well over 60 ms. Consistent with the 11/23/2025 note "ECG today: sinus rhythm".

Sinus rhythm at 74 bpm with a P wave before every QRS, PR ~186 ms (upper normal). QRS 96 ms with no bundle branch block, axis about +55 degrees, QTc (Bazett) ~412 ms. Only ECG in the chart, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus tachycardia at 112 bpm, regular (RR 536-540 ms), with a P wave before each QRS, PR ~165 ms. QRS 102 ms - no complete bundle branch block despite very tall precordial voltages - axis about +37 degrees, QTc (Bazett) ~383 ms. Prior ECG 7/4/2022 was also sinus at 115 bpm with QTc ~385 ms: no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc. Note the coded atrial flutter history is not evident on either tracing.

Sinus rhythm at 61 bpm with one ventricular ectopic beat and compensatory pause. Every sinus QRS is preceded by a broad P wave with a prolonged PR of about 215 ms - first-degree AV block. QRS 104 ms (no complete bundle branch block), frontal axis about -25 to -30 degrees (borderline normal/left). The T wave is broad and late: QT ~520 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~528 ms, i.e. markedly prolonged; she is not on a QT watch-list drug, but this deserves attention. No prior ECG for comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 69 bpm, regular, with a (negative in lead II) P wave before each QRS and PR ~145 ms. QRS 92 ms with no bundle branch block. Net QRS forces are directed superiorly and rightward with an axis of about -172 degrees (extreme axis deviation; lead/limb reversal should be excluded). QTc (Bazett) ~365 ms. Only ECG in the chart. Recorded 4/29/2026, 19 days after escitalopram was started, i.e. outside the required 14-day window.

Sinus rhythm at 70 bpm, regular, P wave before every QRS with PR ~155 ms. QRS is slightly widened at 118 ms with a small terminal r in V1 (incomplete right bundle branch pattern - below the 120 ms threshold for complete block). Axis about +45 degrees. QT ~480 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~520 ms - prolonged, on citalopram 40 mg daily. Prior ECG 6/17/2020 was sinus at 132 bpm with QTc ~413 ms, so QTc has increased by more than 100 ms.

Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, regular, with a P wave before each QRS (PR ~150 ms). QRS is 126 ms with a terminal positive deflection in V1 and terminal S waves in I and V6 - complete right bundle branch block. Axis about +50 degrees. The T wave is enormous and extremely prolonged, still repolarising when the next P wave arrives: QT is roughly 750 ms, giving a Bazett QTc of about 800 ms - grossly prolonged in a patient on escitalopram (flagged separately for prescriber review). Only ECG in the chart, so no comparison.

Sinus bradycardia at 54 bpm (RR 1112-1160 ms) with two late ectopic beats; P waves precede the sinus QRS complexes with PR ~176 ms. QRS 94 ms, axis about -5 degrees, QTc (Bazett) ~358 ms. Prior ECG 12/13/2018 was sinus at 66 bpm with PR ~200 ms, QRS 104 ms and QTc ~374 ms: rhythm unchanged, no new bundle branch block, QTc change <60 ms.

Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, PR 128 ms, QRS 92 ms, axis about +45 degrees. The T wave is markedly late and broad (peak ~360 ms after the R wave): QT ~475 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~506 ms - above 500 ms. The prior tracing (11/23/2022) had QTc ~342 ms at 75 bpm, so QTc has increased by well over 60 ms while on escitalopram; flagged for prescriber review.

Sinus tachycardia at 141 bpm: the RR intervals are regular (402-454 ms) and a single P wave of identical morphology precedes every QRS (PR ~120 ms); there is one atrial deflection per ventricular beat, so this is not 2:1 flutter. QRS 84 ms, axis about 0 degrees, QTc (Bazett) ~397 ms. Two days earlier (7/11/2022) the rhythm was atrial fibrillation with an irregularly irregular response at ~112 bpm, so the atrial fibrillation has resolved (converted to sinus).

Sinus rhythm at 82 bpm, regular, with a P wave before each QRS (PR ~158 ms). QRS 104 ms - slightly wide but below the threshold for bundle branch block - axis about +30 degrees, QTc (Bazett) ~425 ms. Only ECG in the chart.

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm, perfectly regular (RR 492-500 ms) with a P wave before each QRS (PR ~135 ms). QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block, axis about +65 degrees, QTc (Bazett) ~397 ms. This is the only ECG in the chart, so no comparison is possible.

Sinus rhythm at 102 bpm with PR 140 ms, QRS 90 ms, axis about +59 degrees and QTc (Bazett) ~397 ms. Identical to the tracing recorded 34 seconds earlier (100 bpm, QTc ~391 ms): same rhythm, no conduction abnormality and no significant QTc change.

Sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm, regular, with P waves before every QRS (PR ~168 ms). QRS 92 ms, axis about +36 degrees, QT ~420 ms with QTc (Bazett) ~391 ms. Prior ECG 5/22/2023 also sinus rhythm (57 bpm with one atrial ectopic beat, QTc ~377 ms): no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm (RR 492-496 ms) with a P wave before each QRS, PR ~130 ms. QRS has narrowed to 96 ms with only a small terminal r in V1 (incomplete right bundle branch pattern, not a complete block); net QRS forces are rightward, axis about +137 degrees (right axis deviation). QTc (Bazett) ~400 ms. On the earlier tracing the same morning (01:33) there was complete right bundle branch block with QRS 160 ms and QTc ~442 ms, so the bundle branch block has resolved and QTc changed by less than 60 ms.

Sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with one early (ectopic) beat and compensatory pause; P waves precede the sinus beats with PR ~176 ms. QRS 98 ms, axis about +66 degrees. The T wave is broad and late: QT ~500 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~510 ms. Prior ECG 6/7/2025 showed sinus bradycardia at 47 bpm with QTc ~398 ms, so QTc has risen by >100 ms after amiodarone was started on 11/10/2025.

Atrial fibrillation: no P waves are identifiable anywhere in the cycle and the ventricular response is irregularly irregular (RR 386-1092 ms, mean rate ~102 bpm). No measurable PR interval. QRS 82 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -55 degrees (left axis deviation). QTc (Bazett) ~415 ms using the median RR. No earlier ECG for comparison.

arguments.explanation: Sinus rhythm at 91 bpm, regular, with a biphasic P wave in V1 before every QRS and PR ~150 ms. QRS 82 ms, no bundle branch block, frontal axis about -10 to -20 degrees (normal). QTc (Bazett) ~398 ms. Prior ECG 5/16/2021 was sinus at 87 bpm with PR ~146 ms and QTc ~373 ms: no change in rhythm or conduction and QTc change <60 ms.

items.explanation: 80-year-old woman with persistent atrial fibrillation documented at every cardiology clinic visit (most recently 5/28/2026). CHA2DS2-VASc 9 (CHF/hypertensive heart disease with heart failure, hypertension, age >=75 = 2, diabetes, prior cerebral infarction/TIA = 2, coronary atherosclerosis and old MI, female). No anticoagulant is ordered or listed as a current medication - she takes only aspirin 81 mg and atorvastatin - so guideline-recommended oral anticoagulation is missing and needs review.

On citalopram 40 mg daily (current order 5/29/2026; 40 mg also exceeds the usual maximum for QT risk). Most recent ECG (11/10/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 70 bpm, QRS 118 ms, QT ~480 ms and QTc (Bazett) ~520 ms - >=500 ms, so prescriber review is required. Potassium 4.5 mEq/L (1/21/2026); most recent magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (12/1/2023).

On escitalopram 10 mg daily (current order 7/8/2026, QT watch-list drug). His only/most recent ECG (3/8/2026) shows sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with RBBB (QRS 126 ms) and a grossly prolonged, broad T wave: QT roughly 750 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 800 ms (the T wave runs nearly into the following P wave), far above the 500 ms review threshold. Potassium 4.5 mEq/L, magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (4/8/2026).

95-year-old woman on amiodarone 200 mg daily (current order 8/22/2026) with warfarin for atrial fibrillation/flutter. Her most recent ECG (4/27/2022) shows sinus rhythm at 59 bpm with QT ~540 ms and QTc (Bazett) ~535 ms, above the 500 ms threshold requiring prescriber review; QTc also rose by >130 ms from the 4/6/2022 tracing. Potassium 4.1 mEq/L and magnesium 1.8 mg/dL (2/14/2026) - magnesium is at the low end.

Citalopram 40 mg daily was started at the 3/2/2026 cardiology clinic visit. Because the start is on/after 3/1/2026 the revised memo requires an ECG within 14 days (due 3/16/2026). A 12-lead ECG was recorded 3/7/2026 (sinus rhythm, QTc ~358 ms), so the requirement was met.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily was started at the 11/10/2025 cardiology clinic visit. The 9/1/2025 memo applies (start before 3/1/2026), so an ECG was required within 30 days, due 12/10/2025. An ECG was obtained 11/24/2025, within the window, so the monitoring requirement was met (that ECG showed QTc ~510 ms and is flagged separately).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the 2/12/2026 cardiology clinic visit. The start predates 3/1/2026, so the 30-day window of the 9/1/2025 memo applies (due 3/14/2026). An ECG was obtained 3/8/2026 (24 days), within the window, so the requirement was met; that ECG shows a markedly prolonged QTc and is flagged separately.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the 4/10/2026 cardiology clinic visit, so the revised memo requires an ECG within 14 days (due 4/24/2026). The only ECG in the chart was recorded 4/29/2026 - 19 days after the start - so no ECG was obtained within the required window and the requirement was not met by the due date.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the 8/1/2026 cardiology clinic visit; an ECG was required within 14 days (due 8/15/2026). The only ECG in the chart is from 12/25/2025, before the start, and no ECG has been done since, so the follow-up ECG is overdue.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the 8/10/2026 cardiology clinic visit, so an ECG was due within 14 days (8/24/2026). No ECG is in the chart, but the 8/25/2026 telephone note records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 8/18/2026 - inside the window - and the report has been requested but not received. That outside tracing could satisfy the requirement, so completion cannot be determined until it arrives.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily was started at the 9/15/2026 cardiology clinic visit, so an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 9/29/2026. No ECG has been done yet (last tracings are from March 2025), but the window is still open as of 9/24/2026, so the requirement is not yet due.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation (coded diagnosis, repeated in every clinic note). CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (age 65-74, hypertension, coronary atherosclerosis as vascular disease). Only current medication is tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily; no anticoagulant is ordered, so recommended oral anticoagulation is missing. History of hemorrhage complicating a procedure is remote and not documented as a current contraindication, so this needs prescriber review.

At the 9/1/2026 cardiology clinic visit Dr. Kessler documented INR 1.6 and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily. The 3/1/2026 memo requires an INR within 7 days of a dose change by a clinic clinician (due 9/8/2026). INR 2.3 was resulted 9/5/2026, within the window, so the requirement was met.

On 9/10/2026 the anticoagulation clinic pharmacist decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily for a home INR of 3.4 (a dose change permitted by the clinic standing order). An INR was therefore required within 7 days, by 9/17/2026. The most recent INR in the chart is 2.6 from 8/22/2026, so the post-change INR has not been done and is overdue as of 9/24/2026.

71-year-old woman with coded paroxysmal atrial fibrillation and prior embolic cerebral infarction with residual left hemiparesis. CHA2DS2-VASc 5 (age 65-74, female, hypertension, prior stroke = 2). Current medications are carvedilol, metoprolol and famotidine only; no anticoagulant is ordered. Her most recent ECG (3/14/2025) is sinus rhythm, which does not remove the indication in paroxysmal AF.

48-year-old man with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation documented in every cardiology clinic note (most recently 6/12/2026). CHA2DS2-VASc 2 (heart failure - coded acute systolic/congestive heart failure - and hypertension), which meets the guideline threshold for recommended oral anticoagulation in men. Current medications are famotidine and pantoprazole only; warfarin was given during a hospital stay in 2025 but no anticoagulant is currently ordered.

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily was re-ordered on 8/20/2026 (valid through 12/28/2026) and is listed as a current medication, even though outside records reviewed 8/12/2026 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (hemoglobin nadir 6.9, 2 units transfused) with apixaban held at discharge pending cardiology review. The anticoagulant should not continue without that review, particularly with concurrent aspirin and clopidogrel.

Two different oral anticoagulants are current: rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (ordered 7/15/2026, valid to 12/25/2026) and apixaban 5 mg twice daily (ordered 7/15/2026, valid to 12/26/2026). The 7/15/2026 clinic note says the plan was to switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban, but rivaroxaban was not stopped and both appear on the current medication list, giving duplicate anticoagulation and a high bleeding risk.

The 6/10/2026 clinic note states "ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72". Both ECGs recorded that day (17:13 and 19:36) show atrial fibrillation with no organised P waves and an irregularly irregular ventricular response at 142-144 bpm (RR 348-720 ms). The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day tracings.

On escitalopram 10 mg daily (current order 4/23/2026, a QT watch-list drug). His most recent ECG (10/8/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QT ~475 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~506 ms, which is >=500 ms and therefore requires prescriber review per the QT monitoring memo. Potassium 4.1 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (8/23/2025) are normal. Note the 5/14/2024 clinic note describes this same tracing as "QT acceptable".

On amiodarone 200 mg daily (current order 7/29/2026, QT watch-list drug) plus warfarin for atrial fibrillation. Most recent ECG (11/24/2025, two weeks after amiodarone was started) shows sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with QT ~500 ms and QTc (Bazett) ~510 ms, at/above the 500 ms threshold requiring prescriber review. Potassium 4.4 mEq/L and magnesium 2.2 mg/dL (4/20/2026) are normal.
